findings.title: pull_request_target checking out untrusted PR head
findings.detail: This workflow trigger runs with access to repo secrets even for fork PRs, and appears to check out the PR's head ref. This is a known pattern for secret exfiltration / arbitrary code execution from a malicious fork.

findings.title: Unpinned third-party action: actions/checkout@main
findings.detail: Job 'deploy' uses 'actions/checkout@main', referenced by a mutable tag/branch ('main') rather than a pinned commit SHA. If the upstream tag is moved or the repo is compromised, malicious code could run in your pipeline unnoticed.

findings.title: No explicit `permissions:` block at workflow level
findings.detail: Without an explicit permissions block, GITHUB_TOKEN may default to broad read/write access. Best practice is to set 'permissions: {contents: read}' at the top level and elevate per-job only where needed.

findings.title: Self-hosted runner referenced
findings.detail: Self-hosted runners on public repos are a known risk: a malicious fork PR (especially combined with pull_request_target) can execute arbitrary code on infrastructure you control. Verify this runner is not exposed to untrusted workflow triggers.
